advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the 'Stands in for a directory mtime...' docstring back adjacent to `UNKNOWN_MTIME = -1`, above the `_StoredState` type alias.
evidence: 120: """Stands in for a directory mtime that could not be read. Not a real mtime, and so
121: never equal to one and never equal to another unknown: see ``_changed``."""
The docstring text describes a mtime sentinel, not a dict type alias; the `_StoredState` alias was inserted between UNKNOWN_MTIME and the docstring that belongs to it.
advisory.finding: The module-level docstring 'Stands in for a directory mtime that could not be read...' now follows the `_StoredState` type alias, so it reads as documentation of `_StoredState` when it actually describes the `UNKNOWN_MTIME = -1` sentinel defined two lines above. The new type alias was inserted between `UNKNOWN_MTIME` and its explanatory docstring, severing them.
scenarios: A reader navigating to `_StoredState` sees a docstring about mtime sentinels; a reader of `UNKNOWN_MTIME` sees no adjacent explanation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Place the `"""Stands in for a directory mtime..."""` docstring immediately after `UNKNOWN_MTIME = -1` (before the `_StoredState` definition and its own `#:` comment).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion (or a dedicated test) that removing a divergent-name directory with a stored vector leaves no `vectors` row under the reduced ticket id.
evidence: src/rebar/similar/catchup.py:244-247: `keys = {dir_name} | ({recorded} if recorded else set())` ... `drop_vectors(conn, keys)` — the removal path clears vectors under the recorded reduced key.
Commit message: `_drop_removed reads it back and clears the same key SET _reindex clears, from both docs and vectors`
tests/unit/test_similar_tickets_index.py:355-357: removal test asserts only `SELECT ticket_id FROM docs` == [] and `SELECT dir_name FROM dirstate` == []; no `SELECT ... FROM vectors` assertion.

ABSENCE: `search_files` for 'vectors' in tests/unit/test_similar_tickets_index.py returns (no matches); the embedding test file has no 'divergent' test, so vectors removal under a divergent reduced id is untested. Named violating input: dir `1111-1111-1111-1111` reduced to `9999-9999-9999-9999` with a stored vector under `9999-9999-9999-9999` — on removal, a dir-name-only vectors delete leaves the vector stranded.
advisory.finding: The new removal tests do not cover the `vectors`-table clearing that `_drop_removed` performs under the recorded (reduced) key. `test_removing_a_divergent_directory_leaves_no_document_behind` asserts only that `docs` and `dirstate` are empty, never that the `vectors` row keyed by the divergent reduced id was deleted — so reverting `_drop_removed`'s `drop_vectors(conn, keys)` to a dir-name-only delete would strand the vector yet keep these tests green.
scenarios: A divergent-name ticket with an embedded vector is removed; the vector row keyed under the reduced id survives and can still be ranked.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the removal test, after store_vector-ing a vector for `9999-9999-9999-9999`, remove the directory, run catch_up, and assert `conn.execute("SELECT ticket_id FROM vectors").fetchall() == []`.
